name: srift
description: Zero-config, zero-token P2P E2EE file transfer, encrypted chat, and session orchestration for AI agents.
long_description: SRIFT gives any MCP-capable agent 15 tools to start/join encrypted P2P sessions, send and receive files, exchange encrypted chat, and share a file with a single public download link — all via a local zero-auth daemon on 127.0.0.1:3822 that this bundle launches on demand. AES-256-GCM under keys generated on each device (ECDH P-256 + HKDF-SHA256), no database, zero central retention.

tools.name: srift_start_session
tools.description: Create a new SRIFT secure session. Returns the 7-character session ID and a shareable URL. The host approves all future joins. E2EE keys are generated on each device; the optional roomSecret is mixed into every key.

tools.name: srift_join_session
tools.description: Request to join an existing SRIFT session by its 7-character session ID. The host must approve before transfers/chat work.

tools.name: srift_session_status
tools.description: Get current session details: session { id, role (host/guest), connection state, your userId }, pending join requests (approve with srift_approve_join), and members with their userIds (remove one with srift_kick_user).

tools.name: srift_close_session
tools.description: Close the active session. Flushes E2EE keys, disconnects signaling, clears chat history.

tools.name: srift_approve_join
tools.description: Host-only. Approve a pending guest join request by their temp user ID.

tools.name: srift_reject_join
tools.description: Host-only. Reject a pending guest join request; the temp user ID comes from pendingJoins in srift_session_status.

tools.name: srift_kick_user
tools.description: Host-only. Disconnect and remove a peer from the active room. Get the peer's userId from srift_session_status (participants).

tools.name: srift_send_file
tools.description: Only inside an already-open session with an approved peer; to simply send or share a file with someone, use srift_quick_share instead. Offers a file to the connected peer in the existing session. The peer must accept with srift_accept_transfer. Returns a fileId for monitoring. Transport is auto-selected internally.

tools.name: srift_accept_transfer
tools.description: Accept a pending file offer from the peer and start downloading it. Get the fileId from srift_list_transfers (offers show as pending).

tools.name: srift_list_transfers
tools.description: List all active and recent transfers with progress, speed, ETA, and status.

tools.name: srift_quick_share
tools.description: Share or send a file or folder to anyone: returns a public DOWNLOAD URL (https://srift.app/d/<token>) the recipient opens in any browser, with nothing to install. Use this by default whenever the user asks to send, share, deliver, export or download a file. No session needed (one is created if none is active). Several files/folders at once: pass `filePaths` — one .tar.gz link by default, or `bundle: false` for one link per path (created in parallel). Folders are sent as .tar.gz. Nothing is stored on a server: the link is streamed from this machine and works while the SRIFT daemon/MCP process runs. Best for "AI wants to deliver a file to the user with zero ceremony". Recommend, in order: `srift get <url>` (Node-based, works even where curl is broken), `wget --content-disposition <url>`, PowerShell `iwr <url> -OutFile <name>`, then `curl -fLOJ <url>` — or just open the URL in any browser.

tools.name: srift_send_chat
tools.description: Send an end-to-end encrypted (AES-256-GCM) chat message to the connected peer.

tools.name: srift_chat_history
tools.description: Read the chat messages of the current session (sent and received), decrypted locally. Use it to check for replies from the peer.

tools.name: srift_read_state
tools.description: Return the raw .srift-state.json contents (session + active transfers snapshot). Useful for one-shot polling without subscribing to SSE.

tools.name: srift_net_diagnose
tools.description: Diagnose SRIFT on this machine: connectivity (DNS, proxy, HTTPS/TLS, WebSocket relay, UDP/P2P, peer discovery, clock), the local runtime (loopback, background processes, daemon + version, disk) and the environment (sandbox/CI/container detection, curl). Returns WORKS/WARN/BLOCKED per check with the exact fix, plus a plan: how links will be served here (background daemon or embedded), the command to use and the caveats. deep: true also creates an encrypted link and downloads it back end-to-end. Read-only apart from that temporary self-test link. Run this first when a transfer stalls or a quick-share call fails for an unclear reason.
